title: Invasive Ventilation in COPD
keywords: ventilate to the patient's own chronic baseline not PaCO2 40
match extrinsic PEEP to 70-85% of intrinsic auto-PEEP
watch flow-volume waveform return to baseline
sources: Critical Vector — Vent Pocket Guide: Invasive Ventilation in COPD
Standard critical-care references on obstructive-lung ventilation

changelog.change: Added whyThisMatters + clinicalTakeaway (standard Reference Library template, DIRECTIONS_FORWARD §1).
Initial entry — the two key moves (ventilate to baseline PaCO2, match extrinsic PEEP to auto-PEEP) and the monitoring emphasis.

summary: Obstructive physiology like status asthmaticus, but the TARGET is different: return the PaCO2 toward the patient's own chronic compensated baseline, not to 40. And — counter-intuitively — adding a modest amount of extrinsic PEEP eases the work of triggering without meaningfully worsening hyperinflation.
whyThisMatters: The COPD patient on a ventilator has obstructive physiology like asthma but a different endpoint — driving the PaCO₂ to 40 strips their chronic buffering and makes weaning harder — and the one counter-intuitive move, adding extrinsic PEEP, is the one most often withheld.
clinicalTakeaway: Target the PaCO₂ back toward the patient's own compensated baseline, not 40. Add a modest extrinsic PEEP (around 5, or roughly 80% of measured auto-PEEP) to ease triggering without worsening hyperinflation. Use a long expiratory time and watch for auto-PEEP.

items: Permissive hypercapnia to the patient's OWN baseline. A chronic PaCO2 of 55–65 with a compensated pH does not need to be ventilated to 40 — pushing to 'normal' causes a post-hypercapnic metabolic alkalosis (the retained bicarbonate is now unopposed), which impairs weaning and can cause seizures and arrhythmia. Set the minute ventilation to restore the usual pH, not a textbook CO2.

Match extrinsic PEEP to ~ 70–85% of the measured intrinsic (auto-) PEEP. This raises the alveolar pressure the patient must overcome to trigger a breath closer to the circuit pressure, reducing triggering work and missed triggers — without significantly adding to end-expiratory volume. Measure auto-PEEP with an expiratory hold and re-check after each change.
Tidal volume 6–8 mL/kg PBW; rate low enough to allow full exhalation (start ~ 12–16, titrate down if auto-PEEP rises).
High inspiratory flow / short inspiratory time to lengthen expiratory time; I:E ≥ 1:3–1:4.

Bronchodilators, steroids, and treat the trigger (infection, heart failure, PE). Extubate to NIV early — a planned extubation to BiPAP in a hypercapnic COPD patient reduces re-intubation and mortality.

body.text: Monitoring is the same as status asthmaticus — watch the flow–volume waveform for failure to return to baseline before the next breath, and prioritise expiratory time over chasing a normal blood gas. A hypotensive, hyperinflated COPD patient is managed the same way: disconnect, let them exhale, fluid, lower the rate.
